literal: Than a fool's great having-become-intimate friendship, wise people's enmity ten million will be.
translation: The enmity of the wise is ten million times better than the deep intimacy of a fool.
modern: அறிவில்லாதவர்களுடன் கொள்ளும் மிக நெருக்கமான நட்பை விட, அறிவுடையவர்களுடன் கொள்ளும் பகைமை கோடி மடங்கு நன்மையைத் தரும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the value of relationships based on the wisdom of the people involved. The word 'பேதை' refers to a fool, and 'பெருங் கெழீஇ' describes an intense, intimate bond. The poet asserts that even the enmity ('ஏதின்மை') of wise people ('அறிவுடையார்') is ten million times ('கோடி') better than such a friendship. This is because the wise, even as enemies, will act with principles and reason, whereas a fool's friendship will inevitably lead to ruin.
